title: Tenant policy staleness causes geo downgrade and wrong-model routing for mixed-hosted/dedicated tenants
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported degraded performance and incorrect model/region selection between Hosted and Dedicated backends for mixed deployments. Observed behavior: requests from several tenants were routed to a lower-cost economy model in a different region (eu-west) despite tenant policy requiring us-east and a dedicated pool. Impact: elevated latency, higher error rates (model incompatibility errors), and several escalations from two enterprise customers (legal-docs and chat-saas).

Root cause hypothesis (initial): a policy cache invalidation bug allowed stale tenant policy snapshots to be used during a policy merge/rollout window. When runtime policy sync and the new granular per-tenant affinity rules overlapped, the merge logic could return a fallback variant with incorrect region and tier. The bug manifests only when: (a) tenant has a mixed allocation (hosted + dedicated reserved pool), (b) a remote policy patch is applied while routing cache eviction is in-flight, (c) sequence of policy-merge RPCs interleave in a way that one service applies a partial merge resulting in a default fallback to economy-tier and nearest-region heuristic.

Why this is customer-impacting: The fallback to an incompatible model led to generation errors (decoder mismatch) for customers using customized model variants and to degraded SLAs for enterprise contracts. The Dedicated pool owner noticed dropped throughput and spike in latency for pinned in-region requests.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Create a tenant with both hosted and dedicated assignments and a strict region affinity (us-east-1) in policy v1.
2) Deploy a policy patch that adds a new per-route override and triggers a policy-rollout.
3) Simulate routing-service instances A and B where A receives the updated policy but B still has the old cache; induce eviction request ordering that causes B to serve requests during partial merge.
4) Observe routing decision sent to economy model in eu-west instead of dedicated us-east pool; logs show policy_merge() returned fallback_variant:economy and region:eu-west.

Immediate mitigation applied (since 2026-03-11):
- Rollback of the recent policy merge code path to fail-safe deterministic merge (hotfix PR #8743) and short-term config: disable cross-region fallback for tenants with reserved capacity.
- Emergency routing rule pushed: any tenant with reserved dedicated capacity must respect dedicated-pool affinity until full policy-sync confirmed.
- Notified affected customers and enabled per-tenant emergency pinning.

Current status: hotfix merged to canary and observed for 48h. Canary metrics show routing errors reduced to baseline and dedicated pool throughput returned to normal. A full rollout to prod is scheduled after integration tests and a targeted chaos test under staging.

Planned long-term fixes:
- Fix deterministic policy-merge algorithm so it cannot return partial fallback when any upstream rule references dedicated pools (ENG-52994-FIX-MERGE).
- Add a strict versioned policy handshake between control plane and routing instances to ensure policy snapshots are applied atomically; will include monotonic policy version and per-instance ack (ENG-53012).
- Add unit and e2e tests that simulate interleaved merges and verify no downgrade to economy tier for pinned tenants.
- Improve observability: a new routing incident dashboard that surfaces policy version mismatch counts, per-tenant fallback reasons (policy-staleness, capacity, geo), and model-incompatibility errors.

Acceptance criteria for close:
- Canary -> prod rollout for merge fix with 72h of zero regression in routing mismatch alerts.
- New e2e tests passing in CI and added regression test in chaos-suite.
- Postmortem drafted and shared with ops and sales teams; affected customers provided timeline and remediation summary.

Notes on next steps and owner responsibilities:
- Diego Martins (assignee): implement deterministic merge + unit tests, coordinate canary rollout.
- Priya Raman (SRE): create chaos test matrix and run targeted chaos in staging + verify metrics.
- Maya Lopez (Support/CS): confirm remediation communication & customer follow-ups.

2026-03-12 Priya Raman: Canary metrics for routing service for 24h look stable. Detected one residual count of policy_version_mismatch which needs better instrumentation. Adding to ENG-53012.
2026-03-12 Maya Lopez: Customer communications sent (legal-docs and chat-saas). Both requested ETA for permanent fix and confirmation of data isolation. CS to follow up after full rollout.

2026-03-13 Diego Martins: Began implementation of deterministic merge tests. Found edge case with policy fallback comparator where empty priority lists defaulted to lexicographic order; adding test and patch.
